main_text.p: occurro : defectus hic maximus est virtutis gratiæ, quod non possit peccaminosum τὸ[?] nolle consentire, auferre, atque adeo rebellionem expugnare, præsertim cum victoria nostra, & de peccato, mundo, & diabolo triumphus expresse tribuatur divinæ gratiæ robori in scripturis. 1.Pet.1. 5. Phil. c. 4. v. 13. 1. Ioh. 4. 4. Ephes. 3. 16. Juxta enim Arminianos, si posita sufficienti gratia ejusque actione, manet in me τὸ[?] nolle consentire Deo vocanti, procul dubio non vinco Diabolum & peccatum, ut ait Ioannes, quoniam spiritus sanctus per gratiam inhabitans in me est fortior Diabolo & peccato, quippe posito robore spiritus gratiosi, fieri potest ut vincat Diabolus qui est in mundo, & non spiritus qui est in nobis. Si enim non fit ex virtute & robore gratiæ, quod non fit in me non τὸ[?] nolle consentire Deo vocanti, potius quam in Iuda, tum erit a pura natura liberi arbitrii, ideoque victoria naturæ, non gratiæ debebitur : dent adversarii tertium, & causa volens excidam.

6. Ut jam gratiæ efficacia & actualis prædeterminatio magis appareat, notari velim. Quando nos docemus gratiam prædetermi-nantem ex vi sua intrinseca inclinare voluntatem ad τὸ[?] consentire potius quam ad dissentire, id tripliciter intelligitur. 1. Quod gratia efficax impediat impetum & motum obliquitatis & irrectitudinis vitiosæ, quæ libertati extrinsecè adhæreat, & hunc sensum lubens admit-to. Nisi enim Deus actualem duritiem in a-ctibus

page.notes: Greek τὸ before "nolle" and before "consentire" is uncertain: the printed symbol is a small accented tau; read as τὸ, marked [?]. The running head's chapter number is read as "C.ii." and may be "C.ii" with a superscript; marked as read. The initial "occurro" is a fragment continuing from the previous page. "Ephes." is printed with a long s in the source, written with a plain s. The underlining of "Quando" in the scan is not transcribed. Last line ends mid-word ("a-" / "ctibus") and continues on the next page.
